title.en: BASH ↔ 拍 pāi · Abash historical correction
title.zh-Hans: BASH ↔ 拍 pāi · Abash 历史修正

gloss.en: hit or strike violently; crash or smash, depending on context
gloss.zh-Hans: 猛击、狠打；依语境可译猛撞、砸

meaning.en: Cross-language candidate: 拍 pāi — b–p–m–f Consonant-Group Hypothesis / Phonetic-Semantic Candidate, NOT historical cognacy. Standard translation: bash = 猛击 / 狠打 / 猛撞 / 砸. Language Book candidate: BASH → HIT / STRIKE / IMPACT ← 拍 pāi. Related abash means embarrass/disconcert; it is not this mapping.
meaning.zh-Hans: 跨语言候选：拍 pāi — b–p–m–f 辅音组假说／音义候选，不主张历史同源。标准翻译：bash＝猛击／狠打／猛撞／砸。Language Book 候选：BASH → HIT / STRIKE / IMPACT ← 拍 pāi。相关词 abash 意为使窘迫／局促不安，不是本映射。

primary_mapping.mapping_type: Standard translation; separately graded Phonetic-Semantic Candidate bash ↔ 拍

rationale.en: The shared action domain supports comparison. Initial b ↔ p belongs to Jinkai Liu’s b-p-m-f consonant-group hypothesis, not an established sound change or cognacy claim. Candidate, level C, Low confidence; one example does not promote the rule.
rationale.zh-Hans: 共享动作域支持比较；词首 b ↔ p 链接 Jinkai Liu 的 b-p-m-f 辅音组假说，不是已证实音变或同源。维持 Candidate、C 级、Low confidence；不因单例提升规则等级。

summary.en: Independent histories: Merriam-Webster traces abash through Middle English abaisshen and Anglo-French abahir/abaïr, associated with gaping or astonishment. Its modern meaning is embarrass/disconcert. The violent-hit verb bash has uncertain origin. Modern a- + bash “hit” is not an established derivation; no bash–拍 historical relation is claimed.
summary.zh-Hans: 独立词史：Merriam-Webster 将 abash 追至中古英语 abaisshen、盎格鲁法语 abahir/abaïr，早期与张口惊愕有关；现代义为使窘迫／局促不安。猛击义 bash 的起源未定。现代 a- + bash“打”不是已确立派生；不主张 bash 与拍的历史关系。

claim.en: Merriam-Webster documents obsolete bash “be abashed”, from Middle English basshen shortened from abasshen, behind bashful. This is not evidence that violent-hit bash developed into abash. Etymonline proposes Scandinavian or echoic possibilities for violent-hit bash and dates it to the 1640s; Merriam-Webster lists origin unknown and first use 1744. Preserve this source difference rather than claiming a settled date or total unrelatedness.
claim.zh-Hans: Merriam-Webster 记载已废用的 bash“感到窘迫”，其中古英语 basshen 缩自 abasshen，并见于 bashful 的来源；这不证明“猛击”义 bash 发展成 abash。Etymonline 对猛击义提出斯堪的纳维亚或拟声来源的可能，并记作 1640 年代；Merriam-Webster 列起源不明、首见 1744。保留来源差异，不宣称年代或所有同形词之间的关系已完全定论。

claim.en: CUHK analyzes 拍 with a hand component and a phonetic component, while its earliest sense is uncertain. 拍 has Guangyun 普伯切 (aspirated labial, entering tone, 陌 rhyme). 怕 has both 普駕切 (departing tone, 禡 rhyme) and 普伯切 (entering tone, 陌 rhyme). CUHK reports competing accounts of the fear and tranquil senses; none establishes derivation from 拍.
claim.zh-Hans: 拍、怕的字源与历史读音已分别核验；怕有普駕、普伯两套反切，畏惧义与淡泊义的关系仍有不同分析。现代音近不建立派生。

summary.en: BASH → HIT / STRIKE / IMPACT ← 拍 pāi. Initial b ↔ p is a testable mapping within the author’s existing b-p-m-f consonant-group hypothesis. English /b/ and Mandarin p /pʰ/ differ in voicing and aspiration; the rhyme, final /ʃ/ and tone also differ. This is a modern phonetic-semantic candidate, not a historical sound law.

summary.en: ABASH ↔ BASH — Active Association / Cognitive Bridge. Author-proposed by Jinkai Liu; Cognitive / Pedagogical / Creative method, NOT historical evidence. A learner may imagine BASH as sudden physical impact and ABASH as being made embarrassed/disconcerted: PHYSICAL IMPACT → PSYCHOLOGICAL DISCONCERT. This mnemonic is neither a definition of abash nor a claim that embarrassment requires a physical blow. Historical relation (abash / violent-hit bash): unestablished / not derived in this analysis; not a- + bash(hit). IMPACT → STARTLE → FEAR / EMBARRASSMENT is a Cognitive / Experimental chain. 拍 pāi ↔ 怕 pà is a separate Chinese internal candidate; neither the sound resemblance nor an imagined reaction establishes derivation. The photograph scenario is only an editorial illustration, not the author’s original claim.

supporting_cases: Author’s preserved cognitive association only; no historical derivation established
counterexamples: The legacy Chinese gloss is narrowed: modern abash means embarrass/disconcert, not merely surprise.
No regular cross-language sound correspondence has been demonstrated.

Etymonline proposes Scandinavian or echoic possibilities for violent-hit bash and dates it to the 1640s; Merriam-Webster lists origin unknown and first use 1744. Preserve this source difference rather than claiming a settled date or total unrelatedness.

testability.en: Test phonetic similarity and semantic fit separately with blinded controls and independent historical review.
testability.zh-Hans: 以盲法对照和独立词源核验分别测试声音相似度与语义适配。

claim.en: Jinkai Liu’s existing b-p-m-f grouping is applied here as initial b ↔ p in bash ↔ 拍. This case does not prove interchangeability across English and Chinese, and supplies no evidence yet for b ↔ m/f.
claim.zh-Hans: 本例将 Jinkai Liu 既有 b-p-m-f 分组应用为 bash ↔ 拍 的词首 b ↔ p 候选；本例不能证明英汉辅音可互换，也尚未提供 b ↔ m/f 的证据。

supporting_cases: bash ↔ 拍 — candidate positive case; not a validation set
counterexamples: No collected counterexample dataset yet; do not mistake this empty sample for absence of counterexamples.
Unmatched rhyme, /ʃ/ and tone; voicing/aspiration differ.
One selected positive example cannot demonstrate a rule.

testability.en: Pre-register b ↔ p/m/f comparisons, collect positive and negative examples without selecting for meaning, and compare blinded semantic correspondence rate with random and matched-control baselines. Report all cases, uncertainty and held-out results; avoid cherry-picking.
testability.zh-Hans: 预注册 b ↔ p/m/f 比较；不按语义筛样，收集正例与反例；盲评 semantic correspondence rate，与随机及匹配控制基线比较。公布全部案例、不确定性和留出集结果，避免 cherry-picking。

result.en: No results. Collect b ↔ p/m/f positives, negatives and random/matched controls, then compare semantic correspondence rate. A single bash ↔ 拍 case cannot establish the rule.

proposition.en: Literature may connect what appears unrelated; research asks whether the connection reveals a repeatable structure.

project_note.en: Collanguage imagines a bridge through which English and French speech may be heard as musical Chinese in a future spacefaring age.
project_note.zh-Hans: 通语 Collanguage 想象一座语言桥梁：面向未来宇航时代，英语与法语可以转化成高低错落、如音乐般的汉语。

title.en: A Bridge Toward the Spacefaring Age
title.zh-Hans: 通向宇航时代的语言桥梁

text.zh-Hant: 架起語言之間的橋梁，讓我們面對未來的宇航時代。當你聽別人說出英語、法語的時候，由於有通語 Collanguage 所建立的規則與想像，你會自動把語句轉化成高低錯落、如音樂般的漢語，實現一種美好的交流。考慮文化因素，把漢語拼音用於跨語系的語言研究，這就是《語言書》Languagesbook 所探尋和追求的。它可以把兩件原本不相干的事情聯繫起來；在文學與想像中，這種聯繫不必先具備嚴格的歷史邏輯。我在我的葡萄園裡，瑪娜花盛開。
text.en: By building bridges between languages, we prepare ourselves for the spacefaring age ahead. When you hear someone speaking English or French, the rules and imagination developed through Collanguage may let you transform the utterance into Chinese, rising and falling like music, and thus create a beautiful exchange. To bring Chinese pinyin into cross-language-family research while attending to culture: this is what Languagesbook seeks. It may connect two things that at first seem unrelated; in literature and imagination, such a connection need not begin with strict historical logic. In my vineyard, the Mana flowers are in bloom.

evidence_boundary.en: The bridge, musical transformation and vineyard are the author's literary and methodological vision. They do not establish phonetic correspondence, cognacy or the historical segmentation a + bash.
evidence_boundary.zh-Hans: 语言桥梁、音乐式转化与葡萄园属于作者的文学及方法论愿景；它们不能证明规律语音对应、同源关系或 a＋bash 的历史切分。

editorial_notes.en: Active Association Principle｜主动联系原则: A learner or mapper may deliberately connect formally or semantically suggestive expressions as a cognitive bridge, while keeping that association separate from historical etymology.
editorial_notes.zh-Hans: 主动联系原则：学习者或语义映射者可以主动连接在形式或语义上具有启发性的表达，作为认知与记忆桥梁，但这种主动联系必须与历史词源关系分开标注。

editorial_notes.en: Cognitive / Creative method: literature may connect what appears unrelated; research asks whether the connection reveals a repeatable structure. Active Association is not an Evidence / Historical method.
editorial_notes.zh-Hans: 认知／创作方法：文学可以连接原本不相干的事物；研究则负责判断这种连接是否具有可重复的结构。主动联系不归 Evidence / Historical method。

source.author: Jinkai Liu
source.normalization: Original lexical observation and newly supplied author narrative retained; punctuation and the apparent 圆／园 typo normalized only in the edited literary presentation.
source.raw_note: abash，惊讶。拍 pai。惊讶。拍下让人惊讶。架起語言之间的桥梁，让我们面對未来宇航時代。當你聼别人説出英語法語的的時侯，由于有通語collanguage的所建立的规则舆想象，你會自动的把這語句轉成高低错落的音樂版的漢語，实现一种美好交流。考虑文化的因素，把漢語拼音用于跨語系的語言的研究，这就是語言書languagesbook所探寻追求的。可以把两个不搭界的的事情联系，不是非得具备逻辑。我在我的葡萄🍇圆，瑪娜花盛开。

boundary.en: Candidate / C / Low confidence. Initial b ↔ p is a hypothesis within b-p-m-f; no historical relation is claimed. Standard translation remains 猛击 / 狠打 / 猛撞 / 砸. See the linked hypothesis and planned experiment.
boundary.zh-Hans: Candidate／C／Low confidence。词首 b ↔ p 属 b-p-m-f 假说，不主张历史关系。标准翻译仍为猛击／狠打／猛撞／砸；参见已链接假说及未来实验。

gloss.en: to destroy the self-possession or confidence of; embarrass or disconcert
gloss.zh-Hans: 使失去镇定或自信；使窘迫、局促

meaning.en: Active association: bash — Author-proposed / Cognitive-Pedagogical, NOT etymology. Related historical correction: abash means embarrass or disconcert (使窘迫、使羞愧、使局促不安). It is not the bash ↔ 拍 candidate and is not simply a- + bash “hit”. See the independent Historical track and the linked BASH case.
meaning.zh-Hans: 主动联系：bash — 作者提出／认知与教学用途，非词源。相关历史修正：abash 意为使窘迫、使羞愧、使局促不安；它不是 bash ↔ 拍 候选，也不能简单分析为 a- + bash“打”。参见独立历史轨与同一记录中的 BASH 案例。

primary_mapping.mapping_type: Related historical correction / Standard meaning — not a phonetic mapping

rationale.en: ABASH ↔ BASH — Active Association / Cognitive Bridge. Author-proposed by Jinkai Liu; Cognitive / Pedagogical / Creative method, NOT historical evidence. A learner may imagine BASH as sudden physical impact and ABASH as being made embarrassed/disconcerted: PHYSICAL IMPACT → PSYCHOLOGICAL DISCONCERT. This mnemonic is neither a definition of abash nor a claim that embarrassment requires a physical blow. Historical relation (abash / violent-hit bash): unestablished / not derived in this analysis; not a- + bash(hit).
rationale.zh-Hans: ABASH ↔ BASH — 主动联系／认知桥梁。Jinkai Liu 提出；属于认知／教学／创作方法，不属于历史证据。学习者可把 BASH 想象为突然的物理冲击，把 ABASH 联系到被弄得失措／窘迫：PHYSICAL IMPACT → PSYCHOLOGICAL DISCONCERT。这是记忆桥梁，不是 abash 的定义，也不是说窘迫必须由击打引起。abash 与猛击义 bash 的历史关系：未确立／本分析不作派生；不是 a- + bash(hit)。
